title: Session-affine KV merging and token-sparsity planner for compact prefix reuse
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: GPU memory is highly constrained for large multi-tenant inference workloads. We observe that many short-lived prefixes (greetings, instruction snippets, small system prompts) produce KV entries that are individually small but collectively consume significant slab space and increase fragmentation. Current prefix dedupe handles exact matches and coarse coalescing but misses near-duplicates (templated system prompts with variable slots) and session-local repetition patterns.

Goal: Design and implement a session-affine KV merging layer plus a token-sparsity planner that reduces GPU slab fragmentation and increases cross-request prefix reuse while keeping latency overheads within SLO. The solution should: (1) identify and merge semantically equivalent prefix fragments using lightweight canonicalization and slot masking, (2) compact small fragments into shared slabs with an eviction budget per-session to avoid noisy-tenant eviction storms, and (3) coordinate with the continuous batching layer so batch windows preferentially coalesce requests that increase reuse probability.

Non-goals: Global offline re-encoding of model weights, heavy-weight semantic similarity computation, or any approach requiring model changes.
proposed_solution: 1) Prefix canonicalizer: runtime pass to normalize templated tokens (emails, uuids, numeric IDs) to canonical tokens and compute a short fingerprint. 2) Session-affine merge buffer: transient on-GPU region that coalesces incoming prefix fragments for a given session into a compact representation before committing to the shared fragment store. 3) Token-sparsity planner: a small CPU planner that instructs the runtime which fragments are high reuse candidates versus ephemeral (based on frequency, canonical fingerprint entropy, and session affinity). 4) Slab packing heuristic: allocate micro-slabs for canonical fragments under 1KB and pack multiple logical fragments into contiguous storage slots to reduce metadata overhead. 5) Eviction budget: per-session and per-tenant token budgets to throttle writes to the shared fragment pool and avoid noisy neighbors. 6) Continuous-batching hinting: expose optional batch-affinity hints so the router can group requests likely to reuse the same canonical fragments within the same micro-batch window.
acceptance_criteria: Cache hit rate for short prefixes increases by >= 35% on internal chat workload A
Net GPU slab usage reduction >= 18% for multi-tenant 100-node synthetic test
P99 tail latency for text-gen requests increases by <= 5% under baseline throughput
No cross-tenant data leakage: canonicalization must not rewrite or expose tenant identifiers
Feature guarded behind runtime flag and rolloutable via canary
decision_log: 2026-03-03: Chose lightweight canonicalization (regex + token-class heuristics) instead of neural similarity to limit CPU/GPU cost. 2026-03-05: Opted for session-affine merge buffer to keep ephemeral write amplification low; writes to shared store are batched and rate-limited. 2026-03-08: Agreed to expose batch-affinity hint as opt-in by default false to avoid changing router guarantees without explicit rollout.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overzealous canonicalization could normalize real tenant identifiers -> Mitigation: conservative default regex rules and allow per-tenant opt-out; add privacy tests and synthetic leakage checks
Risk: Additional CPU overhead for fingerprinting hurts throughput -> Mitigation: use SIMD-friendly parsing, sample low-frequency requests, and keep fingerprint size small (32 bits)
Risk: Pack/unpack latency for micro-slab fragments increases p99 -> Mitigation: micro-benchmark and inline fast paths for common sizes; fallback to raw fragments when under SLO pressure
Risk: Eviction coordination complexity across dedicated pools -> Mitigation: maintain per-pool budget and central telemetry to tune parameters
testing_plan: Unit tests for canonicalizer and fingerprint collisions; integration tests that validate commit/merge correctness under concurrent sessions; perf tests measuring slab utilization, p50/p95/p99 latencies with and without feature; privacy tests injecting synthetic identifiers to ensure no canonicalized identifiers appear in shared stores; chaos test for eviction storms with multiple noisy tenants.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature behind runtime flag; internal dev cluster rollout (10% of dev traffic) for 3 days. 2) Canary on dedicated infra with low-impact tenants (5 hosts) for 48 hours monitoring metrics in `runtime/cache/pack` dashboard. 3) Gradual expand to 25% then 75% with automated rollback if p99 increases > 8% or canonicalization false positives > 0.5%. 4) Full rollout with docs and SDK hints for batch-affinity opt-in.
